sentences.text: Heard learned counsel for the applicant and learned counsel for the State.

2. The applicant, who is in custody since 06.11.2022, has approached this Court for grant of regular bail in connection with Bengabad P.S. Case No.09 of 2016, corresponding to POCSO Case No.21 of 2023, registered for the offence under Sections 376/ 34 of the Indian Penal Code and Sections 4/ 8 of the POCSO Act, pending in the court of learned Additional Sessions Judge - VIII -cum- Special Judge, POCSO Act, Giridih.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 3. It appears that this applicant has been made an accused for committing rape upon upon the minor girl.

4. It has been submitted by the learned counsel for the applicant that complete set of F.I.R along with its enclosures have been annexed with the present bail application and there is no suppression on her part.

sentences.text: Innocence of the applicant has been claimed and undertaking has been given for participation in the trial.
It has been submitted that F.I.R has been lodged against unknown and the victim girl has not taken the name of this applicant in her statement recorded under Section 164 of the Cr.P.C.
On the above basis, prayer for bail has been made.
5. On the other hand, learned counsel for the State has opposed the prayer for bail and it has been submitted that the medical and forensic report supports the allegation.
6. Considering the above fact, I am not inclined to enlarge the applicant on bail, at this stage.
Accordingly, the prayer for bail of the applicant is, hereby, rejected.

(Rajesh Kumar, J.) Chandan/-
